summary:
Inspected the requested flashlight runtime/config files and the 2026-07-08 SM6 cook artifacts. Best practical answer: the cook artifacts strongly verify a Linux VULKAN_SM6/HWRT-capable package, but they do not prove hardware RT is active at runtime. For live teleop, use the existing examples/flashlight/run.py runtime CVar readback and filter only its small structured SPEAR lines rather than searching Unreal logs.

Primary live check command:
VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json python examples/flashlight/run.py --map cafeteria_500sqft_v2 --live-lighting-mode realistic --flashlight-profile realistic_live_flashlight --scene-light-intensity-scale 0.0005 --movement-speed 600 --disable-auto-exposure --startup-warmup-seconds 3 2>&1 | rg --line-buffered 'Hardware ray tracing requested config|Hardware ray tracing runtime command/readback state|Flashlight ray-traced shadow intent applied|Live lighting mode'

Success criteria in that filtered output: live mode is realistic; hardware_ray_tracing requested is True; readback.has_readback is True; readback.confirmed is True; each requested CVar readback matches value 1. If ray-traced shadow intent says runtime_confirmed=True and applied=True, that additionally confirms the flashlight tried to use a per-light ray-traced-shadow path. If applied=False with skipped_reason='ray-traced shadow API unavailable', HWRT may still be active for Lumen, but that reflected per-light API was not found.

Artifact/config check commands:
RUN=.control-tower/runs/cook_cafeteria_vulkan_sm6_hwrt_20260708T180416Z
rg -n 'status=success|positive_signatures|negative_signatures_absent|runtime_validation|runtime_blocker|runtime_expected_signatures' "$RUN/verification_summary.txt"
rg -n 'GlobalShaderCache-VULKAN_SM6|GlobalShaderCache-VULKAN_SM5' "$RUN/pak_list.log" "$RUN/filesystem_shader_artifacts.log" "$RUN/verification_summary.txt"
rg -n 'VULKAN_SM5|SF_VULKAN_SM5|GlobalShaderCache-VULKAN_SM5' "$RUN/shader_signatures.log" "$RUN/pak_list.log" "$RUN/filesystem_shader_artifacts.log" || echo 'OK: no SM5 signatures found in filtered artifacts'
rg -n 'ShaderAutogen/VULKAN_SM6|format SF_VULKAN_SM6|FPathTracingRG' "$RUN/shader_signatures.log" | head -40
rg -n 'RayTracing|Lumen|TargetedRHIs|bEnableRayTracing|DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod|ReflectionMethod|VULKAN_SM6|VULKAN_SM5' cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Config/DefaultEngine.ini examples/flashlight/run.py

RT option distinctions relevant here: r.RayTracing=True, r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True, Linux bEnableRayTracing=True, and SF_VULKAN_SM6 are build/cook capability settings. r.RayTracing.Enable is the runtime master hardware RT switch; DefaultEngine.ini leaves it 0 by default but enables on-demand toggling, and run.py realistic mode sets it to 1 unless --disable-hardware-ray-tracing is passed. Lumen GI/reflections are enabled by r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod=1 and r.ReflectionMethod=1; that means Lumen, not necessarily HWRT. Lumen HWRT requires r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing=1 plus the reflection/SPG HWRT CVars read back as 1. Lumen reflections HWRT is specifically r.Lumen.Reflections.HardwareRayTracing=1. Flashlight ray-traced shadows are only an intent path: run.py waits for HWRT CVar readback confirmation, then tries reflected USpotLightComponent ray-traced-shadow setters/properties. Path tracing is separate/offline/editor-oriented; seeing FPathTracingRG compiled proves SM6/RT shader permutations exist, not that live teleop is using the path tracer. Software Lumen can run without hardware RT using screen traces and distance-field paths; therefore Lumen-on alone is not a hardware RT confirmation.

Read examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py and identified per-light ray-traced shadow intent setters/properties and readback fields.
Read cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Config/DefaultEngine.ini and identified project-level HWRT, Lumen, SM6, and Linux target settings.
Read .control-tower/runs/cook_cafeteria_vulkan_sm6_hwrt_20260708T180416Z/verification_summary.txt, pak_list.log, shader_signatures.log, and related artifact logs referenced by the summary.
Checked result packet schema and made no file modifications.

findings.message: DefaultEngine.ini enables HWRT capability with r.RayTracing=True and r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True, allows runtime toggling with r.RayTracing.EnableOnDemand=1, but defaults r.RayTracing.Enable=0. Linux target settings remove SF_VULKAN_SM5, add SF_VULKAN_SM6, and set bEnableRayTracing=True.

examples/flashlight/run.py realistic live mode appends/applies Lumen GI/reflection commands plus these HWRT CVars unless --disable-hardware-ray-tracing is used: r.RayTracing.Enable=1, r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing=1, r.Lumen.Reflections.HardwareRayTracing=1, r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.HardwareRayTracing=1, r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.ShortRangeAO.HardwareRayTracing=1.

run.py already has the most practical runtime proof: read_hardware_ray_tracing_runtime_state uses unreal_service.find_console_variable_by_name and getter methods, then reports readback.confirmed=True only if the requested HWRT CVars are readable and match value 1.

The 2026-07-08 cook artifact confirms SM6 packaging: verification_summary reports success, shader_signatures.log contains VULKAN_SM6 shader autogen and SF_VULKAN_SM6 jobs, pak_list.log contains Engine/GlobalShaderCache-VULKAN_SM6.bin, and the filtered SM5 grep returned no matches.

Cook/package checks are necessary but not sufficient for live HWRT. They prove the build contains the SM6 shader platform and RT-capable permutations, not that the running process selected hardware RT or that Vulkan/device support accepted the CVars.

The same verification_summary says runtime_validation=not_attempted because DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY were empty; prior exact live validation on this host failed before RPC startup. Live confirmation still requires a display-capable session.

Path tracing should be treated as a separate offline/editor rendering path. FPathTracingRG in shader_signatures.log is useful evidence that path-tracing permutations compiled under SM6, but it is not proof that live flashlight teleop is path tracing or using HWRT for Lumen.

follow_up_recommendations: For live teleop, run the filtered primary command and check only the small structured lines. Do not rely on nvidia-smi alone; it can show GPU use but not RT-core or Lumen HWRT activity.

If the filtered runtime readback shows has_readback=False, the SPEAR Unreal service reflection path cannot verify CVars in that build/session; fall back to targeted Unreal CVar console queries or add a tiny explicit readback print in a separate validation script before changing runtime behavior.

If confirmed=True but flashlight ray-traced shadow intent is not applied, distinguish that from Lumen HWRT failure: it means the per-light reflected API was not found or set, while Lumen hardware RT may still be active.
Keep the artifact checks as a preflight: SM6/global shader cache present and SM5 absent are good package sanity checks before attempting live runtime validation.
memory_worthy: SPEAR flashlight realistic live mode already contains runtime HWRT CVar readback; use filtered SPEAR log labels to confirm without searching giant Unreal logs.
The 2026-07-08 cafeteria cook artifact is SM6-positive but runtime validation was not attempted due missing display variables.
